description: Flat 8 m street tile textured as a straight two-lane carriageway with a sidewalk band down each side -- one quad, one PBR texture set.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Square section of straight two-lane asphalt street, raised concrete sidewalk down both sides with a chamfered kerb, dashed centre line, flush rectangular storm drain grate set into one kerb line Materials: Patched grey-black asphalt with tar seams and pothole repairs, chalky white and yellow worn paint markings, stained pale concrete sidewalk slabs, chipped kerb edges, rust staining around the drain grate.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

name: Road Straight Tile
notes: One flat quad, 8 x 8 m, lying in the ground plane at y=0 -- two triangles, one geometry, one draw call, one PBR material, and nothing else. The entire street reads out of the texture: carriageway, lane markings, kerb line, sidewalk slabs, drain grates and manhole covers are painted into the maps, never built. The earlier procedural version of this tile modelled a raised 0.15 m kerb and sidewalk and it did not work, so the flat quad replaces it outright -- there is no kerb to step up onto and a player walks the sidewalk band at road level. Budget overridden explicitly to 2 triangles / 1 draw call / 1 material / 1 unique geometry instead of the hero2x its 8 m footprint would derive: footprint drives the class, but there is no geometry here to spend a class budget on. Quality comes entirely from a high-end PBR texture generator -- albedo, roughness, normal and AO at photoreal fidelity matched to the reference plate -- and not from mesh detail; that is the whole bet of this piece. Fit is the one hard requirement: the footprint is exactly 8 x 8 m on the kit's 8 m grid, which is also the frontage of the kit's shop buildings so a tile row lines up with a shophouse row; the pivot is base-center so tiles snap on 8 m centres; and every road-facing edge carries the same band profile -- 1.25 m sidewalk, 5.5 m two-lane carriageway, 1.25 m sidewalk. Any tile edge must therefore meet any other, and the texture has to be edge-matched to the rest of the set at those band boundaries: asphalt tone, kerb-line position and sidewalk slab coursing must continue across a seam without a visible join. No destruction groups: a road tile is static level geometry, not a breakable. This is the plain repeating piece of the kit and will be instanced far more heavily than any other tile -- forty on screen at once is normal -- which is exactly why it is a single quad: forty of these is forty draw calls off one shared geometry and one shared material, and an InstancedMesh collapses it further. It carries no crossing, no junction and no branch; the storm drain is painted flush into the side band so nothing catches a player. Rotationally symmetric end to end, so it drops in at either of two orientations.
